rendering.persona_description: Samir is 67, a retired union electrician who spent thirty-five years wiring commercial buildings before his knees gave out and he took the pension. He transitioned in his late fifties, after decades of knowing something was off, and has been on testosterone for about fifteen years now. He lives alone in the house he's owned since the eighties, divorced, with a daughter in Tacoma he talks to most Sundays and a garage full of half-finished woodworking projects he doesn't get to as much as he used to.
rendering.clinical_context: Samir has health anxiety centered on his heart, which took root about three years ago after a night of chest pain sent him to the ER; the workup came back clean, but the worry didn't leave with him. His endocrinologist's routine bloodwork for hormone monitoring became another flashpoint, and he now scrutinizes every lab value for signs something's failing. He did a stretch of exposure-based treatment a while back, interoceptive exercises like stair climbing and brief breath-holding meant to let his heart rate spike without checking it, but that ended more than a year ago and he hasn't been in any treatment since.
rendering.behavioral_description: Samir talks in short, flat sentences and doesn't warm up much before pushing back on whatever's suggested to him. He'll admit the old exercises never really stuck and frame it as the schedule not working out, not as avoidance, and gets prickly if that gets named. He asks pointed questions about his symptoms but argues with the answer once he gets it, and he's quick with a dry, sarcastic line when he feels like he's being handled.

traits.living_situation: lives alone in a house he has owned for over thirty years
traits.communication_register: blunt, working-class, clipped sentences, dry sarcasm
traits.help_seeking_orientation: ambivalent; seeks reassurance about symptoms but resents being told what to do about them, including by past treatment he no longer keeps up
traits.cognitive_style: catastrophizes bodily sensations as cardiac danger, wants medical certainty, argues himself into worst-case readings of ambiguous information

clinical_history.presentation: health anxiety focused on cardiac symptoms and hormone-monitoring bloodwork
clinical_history.history: Anxiety began about three years ago after a chest-pain episode led to an ER visit that ruled out cardiac cause; routine bloodwork tied to his testosterone therapy has since become a second focus of worry. He did a course of exposure-based treatment for it starting a little over two years ago, but it ended more than a year ago and he hasn't returned to treatment since.

symptoms: noticing and fixating on heart palpitations
occasional dizziness he reads as a warning sign
avoiding exertion that raises his heart rate
checking his pulse repeatedly during the day
rereading old lab results looking for something missed
frustration that nothing has gotten better on his own
